As of 255 AM EDT Wednesday...

KEY MESSAGE 1...Very warm temperatures will easily challenge and 
likely break high temperature records across the region this 
afternoon. 

1020mb high pressure dominates the local weather pattern this 
morning. A cold front extends from low pressure over NY to the W/SW 
into the Ohio Valley and Great Lakes. Strong upper ridging is 
centered over the Gulf Coast but is extending to the NE with rising 
heights aloft over the Mid-Atlantic. A weak shortwave trough is 
currently clipping NE portions of the area, with mostly just a 
temporary increase in clouds but a few light returns have been noted 
on radar over the last few hours. These clouds and any lingering 
light rainfall will move offshore over the next few hours. 

The main weather story today will be the well above normal 
temperatures. Heights aloft hold steady or rise slightly through the 
day while low level flow will continue out of the W and SW. Clear or 
mostly clear skies and some downslope compressional warming will 
combine for high temps in the upper 80s to low 90s across the 
region. Blended guidance continues to be 2-4 degrees below the 
statistical guidance. Will go with highs 90-93 degrees for inland 
locales with mid/upper 80s for the Eastern Shore. These values are 
well above the record temps for the day at all of our long term 
climate sites (which are 86-87 degrees, all set in 1975). See the 
Climate section below for site-specific data. Forecast soundings 
show ample dry air aloft, however, which will allow dew points to 
mix out into the low/mid 60s this afternoon and keep the heat from 
feeling too oppressive. Clouds will increase across the N this 
evening as the aforementioned cold front creeps slowly south.


KEY MESSAGE 2...A cold front drops southward Thursday with cooler 
temperatures for most of the area. 

A cold front will approach the region from the N tonight and is 
forecast to cross the local area early Thursday. High pressure over 
the Great Lakes will translate eastward and allow for a CAD wedge to 
develop over much of the area. Have continued the trend of lowering 
temperatures vs the blended guidance with widespread clouds forecast 
over the northern 2/3 of the area by early afternoon with NE/onshore 
flow. Latest guidance continues to show the potential for some light 
isentropic lift across the northern counties Thursday. QPF still 
looks quite meager with a few hundredths to perhaps a tenth of an 
inch forecast. High temperatures now range from the mid 60s N to the 
low and mid 70s from Richmond S. Areas near and south of the VA/NC 
border may still make it into the upper 70s to low 80s with thicker 
cloud cover arriving a few hours later than points N. Temps will not 
follow the typical diurnal curve over much of the area with highs 
likely to occur in the morning or early afternoon.   


KEY MESSAGE 3...Warm and breezy Friday with a few showers before 
much cooler temperatures arrive this weekend. 

A deep upper trough is forecast to dig across the Great Lakes 
Thursday night into Friday with a strengthening surface low over the 
Ohio Valley. Southerly flow ahead of this feature will allow the 
front to lift back northward as a warm front Friday morning. High 
temps rebound into the low 80s N with mid and upper 80s S. It will 
become breezy out of the SW by Friday afternoon. Some showers and 
thunder are also possible, primarily across NE portions of the area 
Friday afternoon. Rapidly deepening low pressure will translate NE 
into New England on Friday with a strong cold front extending back 
to the southwest. This front will cross the local area Friday 
evening into early Saturday with significant cold advection moving 
into the region. Some additional precip is possible along and ahead 
of the frontal passage, mainly over the eastern half of the area 
before sunrise. QPF does not look nearly as impressive as a front of 
this strength would suggest. Gusty winds are likely to continue into 
the Friday overnight period and could reach 35-40 mph immediately 
along and behind the front. While kinematic fields will be favorable 
for storm organization, lack of deeper moisture/instability will 
limit the potential for strong to severe convection (or even much 
thunder) across the region.

Strong (1035mb+) high pressure builds into the region behind the 
front with upper troughing remaining over the eastern CONUS, 
resulting in well below normal temperatures this weekend. Afternoon 
highs likely struggle to get out of the 50s across the northern half 
of the CWA despite mostly sunny skies. Low 60s are forecast for the 
southern half of the area. It will also remain quite breezy on 
Saturday with gusts 25-30 mph, and especially near the coast where 
winds could gust 30-35 mph. Overnight low temps tumble into the mid 
to upper 30s in the Piedmont with low to mid 40s for the remainder 
of the area Saturday night. Upper 30s and low 40s are forecast
